Subject: Pilot request: reserved lane for SigmaWorks POC

Hi Mina —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our engineering team is comfortable moving to a short POC to validate latency and cost on your Dedicated offering before we commit to a longer reservation. High level ask: we need a reserved lane (isolated GPU capacity) for a two-week window to run our model sweep and latency-sensitive tests.

Rough requirements from our side:
- Target window: week of July 6 — July 19 (2 weeks)
- Capacity: roughly equivalent to 8x A100 (we can run across <8> instances concurrently)
- Expected qps profile: low concurrency but frequent short-lived requests (p50 latency target <120ms per token)
- We may also need the ability to burst +2 instances for scheduled sweeps

Can Redwood confirm availability, estimated cost for a short reserved lane, and whether we need any contract amendments (MSA/PO) or a one-off autoscale exception? Procurement is cc'd (procure@sigmaworks.com).

Thanks — Sarah

Subject: RE: SigmaWorks reserved lane scheduling & capacity confirmation

Team — quick context: SigmaWorks is a strategic mid-market account; goal is a 2-week dedicated pilot that, if successful, will convert to a 6-12 month Reserved capacity commit. Procurement is already asking for a simple MSA + PO path and an estimate we can surface today.

Options we should size (please reply with preferred option & engineering caveats):
1) Persistent reserved lane: carve out 8x A100-equivalent for the full 2 weeks. Simpler billing, predictable latency, but higher short-term cost.
2) Hybrid: reserve 6 persistent slots + allow 2 burst slots controlled by an autoscale exception for scheduled sweeps. Lower baseline cost, requires ops runbook to enable bursts.

Attached: pilot_capacity_requirements.xlsx (matrix with expected token volumes).

What I need from engineering/ops: rough $$/day for option 1 and option 2 (include any one-time setup/ops overhead), and whether the burst approach requires a change to our autoscaling guardrails (quota increase or temporary override). Also note any risk of noisy-neighbor if we don't fully isolate.

Thanks — Aditya
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 08:35:00 -0700
Subject: RE: SigmaWorks reserved lane scheduling & capacity confirmation

Folks — readout from infra perspective. TL;DR: hybrid approach is our recommendation for this POC. Details below.

Constraints/assumptions:
- A100-equivalent slots counted as 1 unit each (we map to our internal pool flavors).
- Two-week window means persistent allocations must be provisioned ~48 hours before start to avoid provisioning queue delays.
- Autoscaling guardrail: currently max burst above reserved pool requires an approved exception due to shared pool safety checks. Approvals take up to 24 hours once submitted via quota portal.

Recommended plan (hybrid):
- Reserve 6 persistent A100 slots for July 6 — July 19.
- Pre-approve a temporary autoscale exception to allow +2 burst slots during two scheduled sweep windows (we will coordinate exact timestamps). The exception will be scoped to SigmaWorks' project id and expire at the end of the pilot window.
- Ops overhead: 2 hours of runbook prep + 1 hour on-call time per scheduled burst event.
- Risk: if exception not approved in time, bursts will fail to provision; we need procurement to accept a contingency start date or sign the pre-approval authorization.

Estimated cost (ballpark, final requires finance):
- Option 1 (8 persistent): $3,200/day
- Option 2 (6 persistent + 2 burst): $2,450/day + one-time ops setup $500

Attachments: reserved_lane_runbook.md (draft); quota request template link: https://internal.redwood.ai/quota-requests/submit

Action items:
- Laura: confirm billing / discount for a two-week pilot so Aditya can present a firm number to SigmaWorks.
- Dev: validate that model qps profile in the attached spreadsheet maps to our concurrency model (I think we’re fine but want confirmation).
- Mina/Aditya: ask SigmaWorks procurement to sign the attached MSA draft or approve the PO path so we can trigger provisioning.

— Marcus
Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot request: reserved lane for SigmaWorks POC

Sarah — thanks for the quick turnaround. Based on internal review we propose the hybrid approach below as the most pragmatic path to get your tests running on July 6: 

Summary (what Redwood will deliver)
- Reserved: 6x A100-equivalent slots provisioned for July 6 04:00 UTC — July 19 23:59 UTC
- Burst: pre-approved temporary exception for +2 slots during two scheduled sweep windows (we'll confirm exact UTC times; Marcus will own the runbook during bursts)
- Start gating: provisioning will begin once the signed MSA (attached) or a PO referencing deal RDW-3421 is received.

Costs and billing
- Estimated pilot cost (hybrid): $2,450/day (as a reminder, this is an ops-level estimate; final invoice will come from finance). One-time setup fee: $500.

Next steps (timeline)
1) SigmaWorks procurement to review/sign the attached MSA draft (sigma_msa_draft.pdf) OR issue PO referencing RDW-3421.
2) Once we have authorization, Marcus will submit the quota request and provision 48 hours before July 6.
3) Dev and Marcus to run a short pre-flight test with one A100 slot on July 4 to validate latency baselines.

If procurement needs a shorter or longer pilot window we can be flexible; we just need signed authorization to lock capacity. I’ve attached the MSA draft and the pilot worksheet for your review.

Sarah — can you confirm procurement's preferred path (DocuSign MSA vs PO) and whether July 6 still works as a target?

Best,
— Mina
Mina Haddad
Sales Engineer Lead, Redwood Inference
